title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Scripture elect: Rom 5, Eph 2, Col 1 seem to reconcile enemies before faith
pass_a_gloss: There are certain other places which are adduced to prove that our reconciliation with God does not then take place when through faith we embrace the Mediator, but that all the elect were reconciled to God from eternity. Of this kind are Romans 5:10, When we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son. Likewise Ephesians 2:4, 5, On account of the great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in sins, he made us alive together with Christ. Finally Colossians 1:21, 22, You, When you were alienated and enemies in mind in evil works, he has now indeed reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, and so on. From these places it appears that reconciliation does not follow the act of faith, but that God is reconciled to his own even then when they exist unbelieving and enemies to God. For it is not an argument of a placable and reconcilable God, but of one placated and actually reconciled, when he honors humans with such benefits.
pass_b_english: Still other places are brought to prove that reconciliation with God does not begin when through faith we embrace the Mediator, but that every elect person was already reconciled to God from eternity. Romans 5:10 is of that kind: "when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son." So is Ephesians 2:4–5: "because of the great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in sins, he made us alive together with Christ." And so is Colossians 1:21–22: "you who were once alienated and enemies in mind in evil works he has now indeed reconciled in the body of his flesh through death," and so on.

From those places the adversaries infer that reconciliation does not wait on the act of faith. God, they say, is already reconciled to his own even while they still stand unbelieving and hostile to him. Benefits like these, they argue, are not the mark of a God merely placable and reconcilable, but of one already placated and actually reconciled.
source_text: Sunt quaedam alia loca quae afferuntur ut probent reconciliationem nostram cum Deo non tum fieri cum per fidem amplectimur Mediatorem, sed electos omnes fuisse Deo ab aeterno reconciliatos. Hujusmodi sunt, Rom. v. 10. Cum inimici eramus, reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem filii sui. Item, Ephes. ii. 4, 5. Propter multam charitatem qua dilexit nos, etiam cum mortui eramus in peccatis, una vivificavit nos cum Christo. Denique Coloss. i. 21, 22. Vos, Cum eratis alienati & inimici mente in operibus malis, nunc sane reconciliavit in corpore carnis suae per mortem, &c. Ex hisce locis apparet reconciliationem non consequi actum fidei, sed Deum esse reconciliatum suis etiam tum cum illi increduli & inimici existant Deo. Non enim argumentum est Dei placabilis & reconciliabilis, sed placati & actu reconciliati, quando homines dignatur talibus beneficiis.
